literal: Such persons these are to us, of such nature we are [to them], saying thus, even if praised, mean will be called friendship.
translation: Even if one praises a friendship by boasting, 'They are of such great value to us, and we are of such nature to them,' that friendship becomes trivial and loses its dignity.
modern: இவர் நமக்கு இப்படிப்பட்டவர், நாம் இவருக்கு இப்படிப்பட்டவர் என்று பெருமையாகச் சொன்னாலும், அந்த நட்பு தன் பெருமையை இழந்து சிறுமைப்பட்டுப் போகும்.
explanation: This couplet teaches that true friendship does not require boastful words or public declarations of mutual value. When friends start defining and measuring their relationship by saying, 'They are so good to us, and we are like this to them,' the friendship loses its natural depth and becomes trivial ('புல்'). True friendship is an unspoken, deep connection that does not need to be calculated or advertised. Embellishing or praising it with such words only diminishes its true worth.
